headline: The low point and face are both closer to right, but face-to-path still leaks right on average. Half-speed 9-to-3 work isn't sticking, so the prescription shifted to full-speed drills that force rotation rather than ask for it slowly.
facts: 8 Sep session: face-to-path averaged +3.7° (6I) and +4.2° (7I) — still leaking right, though the two smoked shots both had face-to-path near zero.
Slow swings let the hands steer instead of release — the opposite of what the drill is meant to build. Full-speed drills that force rotation mechanically are the fix.
Dynamic lie is 7–9.5° toe down on every club, varies by club so it's real, not a sensor offset. Toe-down bias sits underneath the swing fault — keep them separate.
Best 6-iron: 166.8 m carry, smash 1.42, face-to-path +0.4°. Best 8-iron: 139.1 m, smash 1.39, face-to-path −1.8°. When it's square, it's genuinely good.

drills.d: Heels touching, full 8-irons. Forces body rotation to lead since there's no ground to brace against; arms follow.
Trail hand 3–4 inches down the shaft. Makes flipping the club awkward, so forearms rotate instead of hands.
Alternate: 10-yard draw, 10-yard fade, straight. Full speed. Score on whether it curved as intended — builds face-to-path feel directly.
Watch face-to-path, not face angle. Target under +2°, and negative on the draws.

targets: Lie: separate issue, for the fitter
